finding.claim: Authorization result is discarded in dropTable, so any authenticated user (any role) can reach the DROP TABLE path that requires the dba role.
finding.source: Any authenticated user request to POST /admin/drop (precondition: a user object in request context set by middleware not in this repo)

trace.note: runSQL executes DDL regardless of authorization result

finding.guards_checked: Authorize at api.go:13-20 does return an error but caller ignores it; vacuum at api.go:33-36 shows the correct check pattern; no other gate in this file. Caveat: if upstream middleware admits unauthenticated requests this becomes CRITICAL.

verdict.guard_found: none effective. Authorize (api.go:13-20) returns errors.New("forbidden") at line 19 for non-dba users, but dropTable calls it as a bare statement at line 26 and discards the result. No other check exists in dropTable (api.go:24-29) or in the file, and vacuum (api.go:33-35) is the correct pattern that dropTable lacks.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches: /admin/drop routes to dropTable (api.go:44), userFrom at api.go:25, the Authorize error is discarded at api.go:26, and runSQL("DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t")) executes at api.go:27. Any authenticated user with a context user object reaches the DDL, because userFrom (api.go:22) panics without one, so only authenticated users get past it; the middleware that sets that object is outside this repo, but the missing check in this file is enough to confirm the finding.

finding.claim: Raw form value t is concatenated into a DROP TABLE statement, enabling arbitrary table drops and possibly stacked statements.
finding.source: r.FormValue("t") (query string or form body) at api.go:27
finding.sink: runSQL at api.go:27 (stub at api.go:41; execution behavior unverified)

trace.note: runSQL is an empty stub in this repo

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, identifier quoting, or validation on t. Reachable by any user because of AUTH-1.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 is a bare statement and its error return is discarded, so it blocks nothing. No identifier allowlist, quoting, or validation of t exists on the path from api.go:27 to runSQL at api.go:41. Route-level authentication (AUTH-1) is not in this directory, so no guard for it could be checked.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: api.go:27 concatenates r.FormValue("t") into the DDL string, and the role check at api.go:26 is ignored, so no effective guard exists in this file. But runSQL at api.go:41 is an empty stub, so the DROP TABLE is never executed in this repo and the claimed effect cannot be confirmed; reachability by an unprivileged user depends on the AUTH-1 middleware, which is not in the directory.

finding.claim: Admin routes listen on all interfaces over plain HTTP with no server timeouts, and the ListenAndServe error is ignored.
finding.source: Network position: any host that can reach port 8083
finding.sink: http.ListenAndServe(":8083", nil) exposing admin routes in cleartext

trace.note: admin routes registered on default mux
ListenAndServe on ":8083" (all interfaces), no TLS, no http.Server timeouts, error unchecked

finding.guards_checked: No TLS, no timeouts, no interface binding restriction in this file. Severity LOW: missing defensive control; primary issues are AUTH-1 and INJ-1.

verdict.guard_found: none. api.go:46 calls http.ListenAndServe(":8083", nil) with no TLS, no http.Server timeouts, and the returned error is discarded. The only controls in the file are Authorize (api.go:13-20) and the checks at api.go:26 and api.go:33. Authorize gates role checks, not transport or interface binding, and api.go:26 discards its result. Neither blocks the cleartext, all-interfaces exposure.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: api.go:44-46 registers the admin routes and calls ListenAndServe(":8083", nil) with no TLS, no server timeouts, and no error check, so any host that can reach port 8083 gets the cleartext listener. This is a LOW-severity hardening gap rather than an authorization bypass, since the authorization defects are separate findings (AUTH-1, INJ-1).

finding.claim: userFrom uses an unchecked type assertion on a string-keyed context value; a request without a user panics.
finding.source: Any request reaching a handler without a "user" context value

trace.note: r.Context().Value("user").(*User) panics when value is nil or wrong type

finding.guards_checked: No nil or ok check. net/http recovers panics per request, so impact is per-request error noise, not service-wide DoS. Severity LOW.

verdict.guard_found: None in the code. api.go:22 has no nil or ok check on the assertion. The only mitigation is net/http's per-request panic recovery, which is outside this code and limits the blast radius but does not prevent the panic. The callers at api.go:25 and api.go:32 do not guard it either, and nothing in api.go sets a "user" context value, so every request reaching these handlers hits the panic.
verdict.reason: The unchecked assertion at api.go:22 panics whenever the "user" context value is missing or not a *User, and dropTable (api.go:25) and vacuum (api.go:32) call it before any authorization, so an anonymous request reaches the panic. The claim is accurate, but impact is per-request error noise, consistent with the candidate's LOW severity. A separate and more serious issue sits next to it: api.go:26 discards the result of Authorize(u, "dba"), so dropTable runs DROP TABLE for any caller, unlike vacuum at api.go:33, which checks the error. That authorization bypass is outside this candidate and should be reported on its own.
